vulns.name: Log4Shell
vulns.summary: The genre founder. A JNDI lookup feature let any Java app on Earth ask an LDAP server for code and then run the answer. CVSS 10.0. The reason the industry now has a vulnerability-naming budget.

vulns.name: Spring4Shell
vulns.summary: Spring Framework RCE via data binding on JDK 9+. Named by pure momentum — the internet was still shell-shy from December. Proof the genre had legs.

vulns.name: Text4Shell
vulns.summary: Apache Commons Text looked at the calendar, saw October, and shipped a string interpolator that reached out to the internet. Textbook third-act behavior.

vulns.name: wp2shell
vulns.summary: Pre-auth RCE chain: REST API route confusion → SQLi → admin account → webshell plugin, on a default install. Forced auto-updates, 62k+ attacking IPs. Lowercase — by now the genre is self-aware.

vulns.name: PHP2Shell
vulns.summary: Two memory-safety bugs in the PHP engine itself, found with AI assistance in August, dropped early on Oct 20. ~70% of the web in scope. Own Wikipedia page, own .com, CISA alert. The genre's Sgt. Pepper's.
